title: Kestrel Valley University System Cloud Database Platform Security Questionnaire
buyer: Kestrel Valley University System (a fictional state university system)
intro: The University System is standardising on a hosted Postgres platform for research and student-facing applications. Some research projects in our medical school hold protected health information, and our campus payment office is reviewing whether card data could ever sit in these databases. Information Security, the Privacy Office and Procurement read every answer. Statements that go beyond your published terms will become contract conditions.
instructions: Answer every mandatory question and give the detail behind each Yes, No or N/A.
Answer Yes only for capability generally available today. Planned, beta or preview items are No, with the stated plan in the comments.
Questions that ask for a commitment beyond your standard terms, or for pricing, must be answered by someone authorised to make it.
Name the plan tier required wherever a capability depends on it.

sections.title: Assurance and certifications
sections.intro: We accept independent attestations in place of our own audit where they cover the service.

questions.text: Do you hold a current SOC 2 Type 2 report, and can we obtain it?

key.detail: Yes. Supabase is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant and audited annually (audit period 1 March to 28 February); Team and Enterprise customers download the report from the dashboard.
key.quote: To access the SOC 2 Type 2 report, you must be a Enterprise or Team Plan Supabase customer.

questions.text: Is your organisation certified to ISO/IEC 27001?

key.detail: Yes. Supabase is ISO 27001 certified; Team and Enterprise customers can access the certificate on the dashboard.
key.quote: Supabase is ISO 27001 certified. ISO 27001 is an internationally recognized standard for information security management systems (ISMS)

questions.text: For your ISO/IEC 27001 certificate, state the edition (2013 or 2022), the certificate number, the certification body, the scope and the expiry date.

key.to_confirm: The ISO/IEC 27001 edition, certificate number, certification body, scope and expiry date; the d1 sources say only that Supabase is ISO 27001 certified.

questions.text: Is Supabase attested as PCI DSS compliant for an environment in which we would store cardholder data in our database?

key.to_confirm: Whether Supabase holds its own PCI DSS attestation (level, scope, AOC); no d1 source states one, and cardholder data in the customer's database falls under the shared responsibility model.

questions.text: Do you operate a paid bug bounty program today?

key.detail: No. Supabase runs a continuous HackerOne vulnerability disclosure program that is recognition-only; paid bounties were announced for 2026.
key.quote: The program is currently recognition-only. Paid bounties will launch in 2026, scaled by severity and impact.

sections.title: Data protection and residency
sections.intro: Research data agreements often name the jurisdiction data must stay in.

questions.text: Can we choose the specific cloud region where each database is hosted?

key.detail: Yes. Each project is deployed to one primary region, and you can choose an exact AWS region; the primary Postgres database, Auth and Storage are hosted there.
key.quote: your project's primary Postgres database, Auth service, and Storage objects are hosted in that region.

questions.text: If we select your "Europe" region, will our data stay within EU member states?

key.detail: No. The Europe general region can deploy to London or Zurich, which are not EU member states; EU-only residency needs a specific EU region.
key.quote: For example, the "Europe" general region includes London and Zurich, which are not EU member states.

questions.text: Will you commit in writing that backups, logs and Edge Function execution for our projects remain in the region we select?

key.detail: Region selection pins the primary database, Auth and Storage; Supabase's GDPR guide says backups, logs, exports, Edge Function execution and sub-processors can affect residency. No written commitment covering them is established.
key.to_confirm: Whether Supabase will contract that backups, logs and Edge Function execution stay in the selected region for this customer.
key.quote: Backups, logs, data exported to external systems, Edge Function execution, and sub-processors can affect your data residency and international transfer analysis.

sections.title: Protected health information
sections.intro: Applies to medical school research projects only.

questions.text: Will you sign a Business Associate Agreement, and on which plans?

key.detail: Yes. A signed BAA plus the HIPAA add-on is required for PHI, and the organization must be at least on the Team Plan.
key.quote: You will need to be at least on the [Team Plan](https://supabase.com/pricing) to sign a BAA with us.

questions.text: Once the BAA is signed, is every project in our organization HIPAA compliant without further configuration?

key.detail: No. Projects must be configured as High Compliance, with Point in Time Recovery, SSL enforcement, network restrictions and connection logging; the Security Advisor flags non-compliant settings, and applying them is the customer's responsibility.
key.quote: When the HIPAA add-on is enabled on an organization, projects within the organization can be configured as *High Compliance*.

questions.text: Is database connection logging enabled by default?

key.detail: No. log_connections is off by default for new projects; HIPAA and high-compliance projects should keep it on, and the Security Advisor warns if it is disabled.
key.quote: Supabase sets Postgres `log_connections` to off by default for new projects.

sections.title: Access and network security
sections.intro: Answer for what is available today and name the plan required.

questions.text: Can our staff sign in to your management console through our SAML 2.0 identity provider?

key.detail: Yes. Organization SSO supports practically any SAML 2.0 identity provider and is provided for Team and Enterprise Plan customers.
key.quote: Supabase supports practically all identity providers (IdP) that support the SAML 2.0 SSO protocol.

questions.text: Does your private connectivity option keep API, Auth and Storage traffic, not only database connections, off the public internet?

key.detail: No. PrivateLink (Team and Enterprise, over AWS VPC Lattice) covers direct database and pooler connections only; API, Storage, Auth and Realtime are not supported over it.
key.quote: It does not support other Supabase services like API, Storage, Auth, or Realtime.

questions.text: Do you provide audit logs of administrative actions taken by our organization members?

key.detail: Yes. Platform Audit Logs record Platform API and dashboard actions by organization members and can be streamed externally; they are available on Team and Enterprise plans.
key.quote: Platform Audit Logs are only available on the [Team and Enterprise plans](/pricing).

questions.text: Will commits that contain your platform secret keys be blocked before they reach GitHub?

key.detail: No. Leaked secret keys are detected after commit through GitHub secret scanning and revoked automatically; push protection that blocks the commit is being worked on with GitHub.
key.quote: We're working with GitHub to add push protection, which will block commits containing secret keys before they reach the repository.

questions.text: Can direct database access be restricted to our campus IP ranges?

key.detail: Yes. Network restrictions limit the IP ranges allowed to connect to Postgres and its pooler, enforced before traffic reaches the database.
key.quote: Each Supabase project comes with configurable restrictions on the IP ranges that are allowed to connect to Postgres and its pooler

sections.title: Service levels, resilience and commercial
sections.intro: We expect around 40 projects across campuses.

questions.text: What recovery point objective can you meet for a production database, and what does it require?

key.detail: With the Point-in-Time Recovery add-on (Pro, Team or Enterprise), the worst-case RPO is two minutes; without it, daily backups are kept for 7, 14 or up to 30 days depending on plan.
key.quote: Overall, in the worst case scenario, PITR achieves a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of two minutes.

questions.text: If a free-tier research project is paused, for how long can it be restored from your dashboard?

key.detail: One year; after that the backup file and Storage objects can still be downloaded and restored to a new project.
key.quote: When a project is paused, users have a 1-year window to restore the project on the platform from within Supabase Studio.

questions.text: Provide a firm annual price for an Enterprise agreement covering about 40 projects on Large compute with PITR on 10 of them.

key.to_confirm: Enterprise pricing for 40 Large-compute projects with PITR on 10; Enterprise is custom-priced.
